paragraphs.title: Trust in God and the Desire to Remain Close to Him

answers: As his light, salvation, and strength
As the captain of a great army
As his guide through the wilderness
easy.explanation: David says, “The LORD is my light and my salvation” and “the LORD is the strength of my life.”
easy.q: How does David describe the LORD at the beginning of the psalm?

easy.explanation: David says that his heart will not fear even if an army camps against him or war rises against him.
easy.q: What does David say he will not fear?

answers: To dwell in the house of the LORD all his life
To lead an army against his enemies
easy.explanation: David says, “One thing have I desired of the LORD... that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life.”
easy.q: What does David desire from the LORD?

answers: Because his enemies are far away
Because he is hiding in a tent
Because the LORD is his light, salvation, and strength
medium.explanation: David’s confidence in the LORD is why he is not afraid of enemies or war.
medium.q: Why is David not afraid of his enemies?

answers: Behold the beauty of the LORD and inquire in His temple
medium.explanation: David wants to dwell in the LORD’s house, behold His beauty, and inquire in His temple.
medium.q: What does David want to do in the house of the LORD?

answers: A source of protection and power
medium.explanation: In this context, strength means a source of protection, security, and power.
medium.q: What does the word “strength” mean in “the LORD is the strength of my life”?

answers: Trust in the LORD leads him to remain near Him
He wants to get farther away from the LORD
He wants to replace the LORD’s house with a military camp
challenge.explanation: Because David trusts the LORD, he desires to stay close to Him and dwell in His house.
challenge.q: How are David’s confidence and his desire to dwell in the LORD’s house connected?

answers: David’s head is lifted up and he praises the LORD
challenge.explanation: David says, “Now shall mine head be lifted up,” and promises to sing praises unto the LORD.
challenge.q: What happens after the LORD protects David from trouble?

answers: From fear, to escape, and finally to surrender
From trust in God, to a desire for closeness, and finally to praise
From war, to victory, and finally to exile
challenge.explanation: David expresses confidence, asks to dwell with the LORD, and promises joyful praise after deliverance.
challenge.q: What progression of thought appears in verses 1–6?

paragraphs.title: Calling to God and Seeking His Face

answers: Have mercy on him and answer him
easy.explanation: David says, “Have mercy also upon me, and answer me.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to do when he cries unto Him?

easy.explanation: David says, “Thy face, LORD, will I seek.”
The verse says, “When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.”
easy.q: What is said about David’s father and mother?

answers: Hide His face or forsake him
medium.explanation: David pleads, “Hide not thy face far from me” and “leave me not, neither forsake me.”
medium.q: What does David ask the LORD not to do?

answers: Seek the LORD and desire His presence
medium.explanation: The expression is a call to seek the LORD, turn to Him, and desire His presence.
medium.q: What does “Seek ye my face” mean in this passage?

answers: He stops speaking to the LORD
He says that he will seek the LORD’s face
He asks only people for help
medium.explanation: When the LORD says, “Seek ye my face,” David responds, “Thy face, LORD, will I seek.”
medium.q: How does David respond to the command to seek the LORD’s face?

answers: His relationship with the LORD matters to him in trouble
He does not want an answer from the LORD
He prefers to depend only on himself
challenge.explanation: David asks for the LORD’s presence and help rather than being left alone.
challenge.q: What does David’s request that the LORD not hide His face show?

answers: The parents receive him, but the LORD forsakes him
The parents forsake him, but the LORD takes him up
The parents protect him, but the LORD hides from him
challenge.explanation: David says, “When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.”
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the verse about David’s parents and the LORD?

answers: Calling on the LORD, seeking His face, and asking Him not to forsake him
Walking a path, facing false witnesses, and singing
challenge.explanation: These verses describe prayer, seeking God’s presence, and asking for His help and faithfulness.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence in verses 7–10?

paragraphs.title: A Request for an Upright Way and Protection from False Accusations

easy.explanation: David asks, “Teach me thy way, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to teach him?

easy.explanation: David asks, “Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies.”
easy.q: From whom does David ask not to be delivered over?

answers: The goodness of the LORD in the land of the living
A new house in the wilderness
easy.explanation: David says he believes he will see “the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.”
easy.q: What does David believe he will see?

answers: So that he can leave the LORD’s house
So that he can hide the false testimony
medium.explanation: David asks to be led in a plain path “because of mine enemies.”
medium.q: Why does David ask to be led in a plain path?

medium.explanation: A plain path is a clear, straight, and level way.
medium.q: What does “a plain path” mean in this passage?

answers: False witnesses have risen against him and breathe out cruelty
medium.explanation: David refers to “false witnesses” and those who “breathe out cruelty.”
medium.q: Why does David ask for protection?

answers: He wants to walk uprightly while facing enemies and false accusers
He wants to hide his path from his enemies
He wants to abandon the way
challenge.explanation: David asks for guidance in a straight way even while facing enemies and false witnesses.
challenge.q: How are David’s request for a plain path and his request for protection related?

answers: David’s opponents are presenting untrue testimony against him
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies people who rise against David with false accusations.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “false witnesses”?

answers: His belief that he will see the LORD’s goodness in the land of the living
His reliance on the power of his enemies
His rejection of every straight path
challenge.explanation: His faith that he will see the LORD’s goodness gives him hope in the midst of trouble.
challenge.q: What strengthens David in the danger described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Wait on the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom is the listener told to wait?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart.”
easy.q: What should a person do in order to be strengthened?

easy.explanation: The verse begins and ends with the command, “Wait on the LORD.”
easy.q: Which command is repeated in the verse?

answers: Courage helps a person continue to wait
Courage removes the need for hope
medium.explanation: The verse connects courage and inner strength with continuing to wait on the LORD.
medium.q: How are courage and waiting connected in this verse?

medium.explanation: The phrase is an encouragement to become strong and courageous.
medium.q: What does “be of good courage” mean in this context?

answers: Continue hoping and do not give up
medium.explanation: The repetition stresses perseverance in waiting and hoping in the LORD.
medium.q: What does the repetition of “Wait on the LORD” emphasize?

answers: David and anyone who needs encouragement
challenge.explanation: The statement is expressed as general encouragement and can strengthen David or anyone facing trouble.
challenge.q: To whom could the words “Be of good courage” be addressed?

answers: Stop hoping when results do not come immediately
Become strong and continue to wait on the LORD
challenge.explanation: The ending emphasizes courage, strength, and perseverance in waiting on the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the central message at the end of the psalm?

answers: It calls for hope and courage in the face of enemies and danger
It replaces trust in the LORD with fear
challenge.explanation: After describing enemies, abandonment, and danger, the psalm ends by calling the believer to courage and continued hope in the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the ending relate to the troubles described earlier in the psalm?
